newsitem.title: FRANCE: Framatome owners not against GEC-Alsthom merger.
newsitem.headline: Framatome owners not against GEC-Alsthom merger.

text.p: The supervisory board of French nuclear engineering group Framatome discussed a merger plan with Franco-British joint venture GEC-Alsthom on Wednesday and did not express opposition to such a move.

In a statement released on Thursday, Phillipe Rouvillois, chairman of CEA-Industrie, said the merger would result in a large industrial project with a range of products allowing it to take on its biggest rivals.
He said it was necessary that existing cooperation pacts, such as with Germany's Siemens AG, be maintained.
He also said that the five percent stake held in Framatome by its staff, via Framepargne, needed particular attention.
The French parties which would be majority owners in the new GEC-Alsthom Framatome combination needed to be able to speak with one voice, he added.
The Alcatel Alsthom representative on the board said the merger proposal had an industrial logic and was not aimed at obtaining Framatome's cash reserves.
On August 30, the French state gave the green light for merger talks between Framatome and GEC-Alsthom, a joint venture of Alcatel Alsthom and GEC Plc.
